subject: crs
topic: The early church: Pentecost, Peter, Stephen and persecution

kept.q: On the Day of Pentecost, what visible sign accompanied the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the disciples as they gathered together in Jerusalem?
options: Tongues of fire resting on each of them
A bright star appearing over the house
kept.explanation: The Bible says divided tongues like fire appeared and rested on each disciple, and they began to speak in other tongues. This is recorded in Acts 2:3.
kept.pidgin: Bible talk say tongue of fire come rest for everybody head, and dem start to speak different languages. Dis one dey for Acts 2:3.

kept.q: Who delivered the first public sermon to the crowd immediately after the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples at Pentecost?
kept.explanation: Peter stood up with the eleven and explained to the crowd that what they were seeing was the fulfilment of Joel's prophecy. This sermon is found in Acts 2:14-36.
kept.pidgin: Peter na im stand up with di eleven disciples come explain say na wetin Joel talk before dey happen. Dis one dey for Acts 2:14-36.

kept.q: According to the account in Acts, about how many people were added to the church on the day Peter preached at Pentecost?
kept.explanation: After Peter's sermon, those who believed his message were baptised and about three thousand souls were added that day. This number is recorded in Acts 2:41.
kept.pidgin: After Peter preach, many pipo believe come baptise, and around three thousand pipo join dat day. E dey for Acts 2:41.

kept.q: Peter and John healed a man who was lame from birth as he begged for alms at which gate of the temple in Jerusalem?
kept.explanation: The lame man was sitting at the gate called Beautiful, asking for alms, when Peter healed him in the name of Jesus Christ. This is found in Acts 3:2-7.
kept.pidgin: Dis lame man dey sidon for di gate wey dem call Beautiful Gate dey beg money, Peter come heal am for Jesus name. E dey for Acts 3:2-7.

kept.q: Who became the first Christian martyr after being stoned to death by an angry mob while Saul of Tarsus watched and approved?
kept.explanation: Stephen, a deacon full of faith and the Holy Spirit, was dragged out of the city and stoned to death for his testimony about Jesus. This event is recorded in Acts 7:58-60.
kept.pidgin: Stephen, one deacon wey Holy Spirit full, na im dem stone kill for outside di city because of im testimony about Jesus. E dey for Acts 7:58-60.

kept.q: In his defence speech before the Sanhedrin, Stephen mainly traced which theme to show that the Jewish leaders had always resisted God?
options: The history of Israel and their repeated rejection of God's messengers
The detailed genealogy of Jesus Christ
Only the miracles performed by Moses in Egypt
The Jewish laws on clean and unclean foods
kept.explanation: Stephen reviewed Israel's history from Abraham through Moses to Solomon, showing a pattern where the people constantly resisted the Holy Spirit and rejected God's chosen messengers, as in Acts chapter 7.
kept.pidgin: Stephen waka through Israel history from Abraham reach Solomon, e show say dem dey always resist Holy Spirit and reject God in-im messengers. Dis one dey for Acts chapter 7.

kept.q: Who was the young man who approved of Stephen's killing and kept watch over the garments of those who stoned him, later becoming a fierce persecutor of the church?
kept.explanation: Acts 7:58 and 8:1 mention a young man named Saul who kept the clothes of those stoning Stephen and approved of his death; he later persecuted the church before his conversion.
kept.pidgin: Acts 7:58 and 8:1 talk say young man wey dem call Saul dey hold di cloth of dose wey dey stone Stephen, and e support di killing before e later convert.

kept.q: After Stephen's death, a great persecution scattered believers from Jerusalem throughout Judea and Samaria. What was one major positive result of this scattering for the growth of the church?
options: The scattered believers preached the word wherever they went, spreading the gospel to new regions
The church in Jerusalem became the only true church and stopped growing
All the apostles were killed and the church disappeared
Christianity was completely banned throughout the Roman Empire
kept.explanation: Acts 8:1 and 8:4 show that although persecution scattered the believers, they did not stop preaching; instead they carried the gospel message to new places like Samaria, which helped the church grow beyond Jerusalem.
kept.pidgin: Acts 8:1 and 8:4 show say even though persecution scatter di believers, dem no stop to preach; instead dem carry di gospel go new places like Samaria, and church grow pass Jerusalem.
